annotation.title_clean: 3D Printing, Artificially Intelligent Robots and Software Inventions, Is Technology Shaking the Reign of IP Law?
annotation.title_en: 3D Printing, Artificially Intelligent Robots and Software Inventions, Is Technology Shaking the Reign of IP Law?
annotation.summary_en: Law journal article examining whether current patent law can handle AI-implemented works, 3D printing and robotics, including inventive step, inventorship and infringement by 3D printers. It concludes the existing regime is inadequate and argues for legal reforms to clarify protection of AI-generated works.
key_provisions_or_claims: Current patent regime is not sufficient for software-implemented works, 3D printing and robotics.
AI-generated inventions strain inventive step, prior art, inventorship and technical contribution tests.
3D printers create a grey area for direct and indirect patent infringement.
Legal reforms are needed to clarify the protection scope of AI-generated works.
